mainTopic: ברירה in rabbinic law, and the תחום of animals, borrowed vessels, and borrowed ingredients on יום טוב
overview: This amud begins by finishing a discussion about whether רבי אושעיא accepts ברירה. The גמרא quotes an earlier answer of רבי יוחנן about two עירובין, which shows that רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law. So the idea of reversing the two opinions fails. Instead, the גמרא explains that רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה only in Torah law and accepts it in rabbinic law, and מר זוטרא rules that the הלכה follows him. Next, שמואל teaches that a fattener's ox may go wherever its buyer may go, while a shepherd's ox may go only where the people of his city may go. The גמרא then explains the משנה about borrowed vessels. A vessel requested before יום טוב follows the borrower even if it was handed over on יום טוב. A vessel borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender, even when the borrower always borrows from him. Finally, the גמרא turns to the woman who borrowed water and salt for her dough. In a story, רבי אבא arrives in ארץ ישראל and finds the sages asking why the water and salt are not בטל in the dough, and his answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting an earlier question about two עירובין and ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes an earlier discussion about איו's ברייתא. If רבי יהודה forbids relying on a choice between two sages because there is no ברירה, why does he allow a choice between east and west?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this teaching: Why is the case of 'here and here' (two sages, one on each side) not allowed? Because there is no ברירה. But then in the case of east and west there should also be no ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting an older question that was asked about the ברייתא of איו about placing two עירובין. It is setting up the next move, which will be an answer from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets a person place one עירוב to the east and one to the west and decide on שבת which one counts, depending on where the single sage comes. But he forbids this when two sages come, one to each side. The question is this: if the reason for forbidding is that we do not accept ברירה, then the east-or-west case should be forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (introduces a quoted earlier discussion)
Retroactive clarification: a later event reveals what was already chosen
Here and here (two sages, one on each side)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not the גמרא's current attack. It is an older discussion being quoted, because the answer to it will be used against the 'reversal' of opinions.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is different about 'here and here' that it is not allowed?
phrases.notes: Two sages are coming, one to each side.

phrases.english: — because there is no retroactive clarification,
then with east and west there should also be no retroactive clarification!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא לְכָאן וּלְכָאן דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to the reversal (איפוך) proposed on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the east-or-west case is allowed if רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in איו's ברייתא that one may place עירובין east and west and decide later, when a single sage is coming.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה forbids the 'here and here' case because there is no ברירה. By that same reasoning, the east-or-west case should also be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the sage had already arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in the east-or-west case the sage had already arrived before שבת. The outcome was already fixed, and the person simply did not know it yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The case is where the sage had already come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the quoted question. In the east-or-west case nothing is decided later, because the sage was already in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sage had already arrived before שבת, the valid עירוב was already set when the עירובין were placed. The person just did not know which one it was. So this case does not need ברירה at all, and that explains why רבי יהודה allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the sage had already come

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The sage had already come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּכְבָר בָּא חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the quoted question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The east-or-west case is one where the sage had already arrived, so no ברירה is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the sage had already arrived, so the outcome was fixed and only unknown.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The east-or-west case seems to rely on ברירה, which contradicts רבי יהודה's rejection of ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the east-or-west case the sage had already come, so no ברירה is needed, and רבי יהודה is consistent.

steps.title: So רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's answer, the גמרא learns that he does not accept ברירה even in עירובין, which is a rabbinic matter. This undoes the reversal that gave רבי יוחנן the opinion that ברירה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see from this that רבי יוחנן does not hold of ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's answer and uses it to attack the earlier reversal of opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן accepted ברירה, he would not have needed to say 'the sage had already come.' Since עירובין is only a rabbinic law, this shows that he rejects ברירה even in rabbinic matters. So it cannot be correct to assign him the pro-ברירה view through איפוך.

phrases.english: Apparently:
Rabbi Yochanan does not hold of retroactive clarification!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא: לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposed reversal (איפוך) of the views of רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן needed to explain the case without ברירה even in rabbinic law. So he cannot be the one who accepts ברירה.

steps.title: No reversal: רבי אושעיא accepts ברירה only in rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the reversal. It explains that רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה in Torah law but accepts it in rabbinic law, so his two statements do not contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really do not reverse the opinions. When רבי אושעיא does not hold of ברירה, that is in Torah law. But in rabbinic law, he does hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on swapping the opinions. It resolves the contradiction in רבי אושעיא's views by splitting between Torah law and rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא's statement rejecting ברירה was about טומאת מת, which is a Torah law. His statement relying on ברירה was about a rabbinic matter. Because the two statements cover different kinds of law, they fit together, and there is no need to change who said what.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא: no ברירה in דאורייתא, but yes ברירה in דרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between דאורייתא and דרבנן is a basic tool used throughout ש״ס whenever ברירה comes up.

phrases.english: Rather: actually, do not reverse,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרֵירָה —
phrases.english: and when Rabbi Oshaya does not hold of retroactive clarification —
that is in Torah law,
but in rabbinic law — he does hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack in step 3 by going back to the original attribution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between Torah law and rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinions should be reversed, so that רבי יוחנן is the one who accepts ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no reversal. רבי אושעיא accepts ברירה in דרבנן and rejects it in דאורייתא.

steps.title: מר זוטרא rules like רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא publicly teaches that the הלכה follows רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught publicly: The הלכה is like רבי אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The סוגיא ends with a practical ruling: we follow רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice this means ברירה works in rabbinic matters but not in Torah matters.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: ברירה works in דרבנן, following רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught publicly:
The law is in accordance with Rabbi Oshaya.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the resolution in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אושעיא: ברירה is accepted in rabbinic law.

steps.title: שמואל: The Fattener's Ox and the Shepherd's Ox
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a fattener's ox follows the feet of whoever buys it, while a shepherd's ox follows the feet of the people of his city.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: An ox belonging to a fattener is like the feet of every person. An ox belonging to a shepherd is like the feet of that city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about how far an animal may be taken on יום טוב. It depends on what kind of owner it has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an animal follows its owner's תחום. A פטם raises oxen to sell to anyone, so from the start of יום טוב the ox is 'ready' to belong to any buyer, even one from another city. A רועה only sells now and then to local people, so his ox follows the walking zone of people from his own city.

keyTerms.meaning: A fattener: someone who fattens oxen to sell them for meat
A shepherd who raises animals mainly for himself
Like the feet of: the object may go only where that person may walk on שבת or יום טוב
The limited area, 2000 אמות from one's place, in which one may walk on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: 'Like the feet of' does not mean the object walks with someone. It means the object's allowed zone is copied from that person's allowed zone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an object's תחום can depend on the owner's intention at the start of יום טוב, meaning who he expects the object to belong to.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
An ox of a fattener
phrases.notes: He fattens oxen to sell to any buyer.

phrases.english: is like the feet of every person.
An ox of a shepherd
is like the feet of (the people of) that city.
phrases.notes: He would only sell it locally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic after the conclusion about ברירה (step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fattener's ox goes with whoever buys it. A shepherd's ox is limited to the walking zone of the people of his city.

steps.title: Borrowing a Vessel Before יום טוב: Isn't This Obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a vessel borrowed on ערב יום טוב follows the borrower, and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who borrows a vessel from his friend on the eve of יום טוב' (follows the borrower). That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first half of the משנה and challenges it: why teach something so obvious? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel was borrowed before יום טוב began, it was already in the borrower's hands when יום טוב started. So it should obviously follow the borrower. The question assumes the משנה would not waste words.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious! A challenge saying a teaching seems unnecessary

phrases.english: One who borrows a vessel from his friend
on the eve of the Festival (follows the borrower).
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה's law about borrowed vessels.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a vessel borrowed on ערב יום טוב follows the borrower.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel was already the borrower's before יום טוב, so the rule seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: The Case Where It Was Handed Over Only on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the borrowing was arranged before יום טוב but the vessel was handed over only on יום טוב. Even then it follows the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the lender handed it over only on יום טוב. You might have said: since he did not place it in the borrower's possession before יום טוב, it should still follow the lender. So the משנה teaches us that it follows the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by pointing to a trickier case. In that case the request was made before יום טוב, but the vessel only changed hands on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think what counts is where the vessel physically was when יום טוב began, which was still with the lender. The משנה teaches that the agreement before יום טוב is enough. The vessel was already 'meant' for the borrower, so it follows his feet.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (for the simple case); it is needed for a special case
Lest you say: introduces the mistaken thought the teaching comes to prevent
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

phrases.english: No, it is necessary

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרוֹ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: where he did not hand it to him until the Festival.
Lest you say:
he did not establish it in his (the borrower's) possession,
phrases.notes: So you might think it should follow the lender.

phrases.english: it teaches us (that it follows the borrower).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is about a less obvious situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the vessel was physically handed over only on יום טוב, it should follow the lender.
steps.terutzMaskana: The arrangement before יום טוב is enough, so it follows the borrower.

steps.title: This Supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Read this way, the משנה supports רבי יוחנן, who ruled that a vessel requested before יום טוב but handed over on יום טוב follows the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן. For רבי יוחנן said: One who borrows a vessel from his friend on the eve of יום טוב, even though the lender gave it to him only on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that its explanation of the משנה matches an independent ruling of רבי יוחנן. So the משנה backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said exactly what step 8 explained. What matters is that the borrowing was agreed on before יום טוב, not when the vessel was physically handed over. Now his statement has a משנה behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him: a source that backs up an אמורא's ruling
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One who borrows a vessel from his friend on the eve of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נְתָנוֹ לוֹ
phrases.english: even though he did not give it to him
until the Festival,
it is like the feet of the borrower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading of the משנה from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a vessel requested before יום טוב follows the borrower, even if handed over on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first half of the משנה, read as in step 8.
steps.whatToRemember: For a borrowed vessel, the key is when the borrowing was arranged, before or on יום טוב, not when it was physically handed over.

steps.title: Borrowing on יום טוב Itself: Isn't This Obvious Too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה, that a vessel borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender, and again asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On יום טוב, it is like the feet of the lender.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of the משנה and raises the same 'obvious' challenge. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב began, the vessel belonged only to the lender and nobody had asked for it. So it plainly should follow the lender. Why does the משנה bother saying so?

phrases.english: On the Festival: like the feet of the lender.
phrases.notes: Quoting the second half of the משנה.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 7, now on the second half of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a vessel borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel was entirely the lender's at the start of יום טוב, so the rule seems self-evident.

steps.title: Even a Regular Borrower: The Lender Thinks He May Go Elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a borrower who always borrows from this lender. Even then the vessel follows the lender, because the lender thinks the borrower might borrow from someone else this time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he is used to borrowing from him. You might have said that the lender sets it aside for him in advance. So the משנה teaches us that it follows the lender, because the lender says to himself: Maybe he will find another person and go borrow from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a regular borrower. One might think the lender already 'gave' the vessel to him in his mind before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken thought is that a regular arrangement means the vessel was meant for the borrower from before יום טוב. The משנה rejects this. A lender cannot count on this borrower coming to him, since he might go to someone else. So nothing was set aside before יום טוב, and the vessel stays with the lender's feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to, accustomed to doing something regularly
He certainly says (to himself): describes the person's likely thinking

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two halves. In step 8 a real request before יום טוב moves the vessel to the borrower's feet. Here a mere habit, with no request before יום טוב, does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Before יום טוב, a vessel follows the borrower only if it was actually requested. On יום טוב it follows the lender, even for a regular borrower.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he is accustomed to borrowing from him.
Lest you say:
he (the lender) sets it in his (the borrower's) possession in advance,
it teaches us (that it is not so),
for he (the lender) certainly says:
Perhaps he will find another person
and go and borrow from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case, plus the lender's likely thinking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With a regular borrower, the lender sets the vessel aside for him before יום טוב, so it should follow the borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lender assumes the borrower might go elsewhere, so nothing is set aside. The vessel follows the lender.

steps.title: Quoting the case of the woman who borrowed from her friend
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a woman who borrowed ingredients from her friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a woman who borrowed from her friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin discussing it. This line is a heading that sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that if a woman borrows spices for a dish, or water and salt for her dough, the food may go only where both women may go on יום טוב. Each item keeps the תחום of its owner, so the mixture is limited by both owners. Here the גמרא only quotes the opening words to point to this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the feet of both of them. The item may go only where both owners may go.

steps.confusionAlert: Only the opening words of the משנה are quoted here. The actual ruling, that the dough is limited to the תחום of both women, comes from the rest of the משנה, which the גמרא assumes you know.

phrases.english: And similarly, a woman who borrowed from her friend.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: spices for her dish, or water and salt for her dough. These are like the feet of both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the borrowed-vessel rulings in steps 7-11 to the next case in the משנה, borrowed ingredients.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ingredients borrowed from another woman make the food limited to the תחום of both women.

steps.title: רבי אבא prays before arriving in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: As רבי אבא went up to ארץ ישראל, he prayed that he would say a teaching the sages there would accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבא went up, he said: May it be God's will that I say something that will be accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about רבי אבא moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל. This sets up the scene for the question and answer that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scholars from בבל who came to ארץ ישראל were tested by the local sages. רבי אבא prayed that his first teaching would be accepted and that he would not be embarrassed. The story now sets up the question he will try to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When Rabbi Abba went up, he said:
phrases.notes: He went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: May it be God's will that I say a statement that will be accepted.
phrases.notes: He hoped his teaching would be accepted by the sages there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that will lead into the discussion of the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not a legal ruling. רבי אבא prays that his teaching will be accepted.

steps.title: The sages ask why the water and salt are not nullified in the dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא finds the sages of ארץ ישראל asking: why aren't the water and salt בטל in the dough? This passage ends as רבי אבא begins to reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he went up, he found רבי יוחנן, רבי חנינא בר פפי, and רבי זירא. Some say he found רבי אבהו, רבי שמעון בן פזי, and רבי יצחק נפחא. They were sitting and asking: Why does the dough follow both women? Let the water and salt be בטל in the dough! רבי אבא said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The sages challenge the משנה's ruling about the borrowed water and salt. The last line, 'רבי אבא said to them', sets up his answer, which continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water and salt are small additions compared to the flour, which is the main part of the dough. Normally a small ingredient is בטל, cancelled out, in the larger mixture. So the dough should follow only the תחום of the flour's owner, not of the woman who lent the water and salt. That is the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different version of the names)
But let it be cancelled out (בטל)

steps.confusionAlert: The sages are not asking why salt and water count as food. They are asking why these small ingredients don't simply lose their identity inside the much larger amount of flour.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question about ביטול in a mixture is the problem that רבי אבא now tries to answer. The story of how the sages react to his answer continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: When he went up, he found Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי וְרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, and Rabbi Zeira,
and some say: Rabbi Abbahu,
phrases.notes: A second version of which sages were there.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
and they were sitting and saying: Why?
phrases.notes: Why does the dough follow both women?

phrases.english: But let the water and salt be nullified in the dough!
phrases.notes: Then the dough should follow only the owner of the flour.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to them:
phrases.notes: This introduces his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? וְלִבְטִיל מַיִם וָמֶלַח לְגַבֵּי עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Within the story from step 13, the sages challenge the משנה rule quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that dough made with borrowed water and salt is limited to the תחום of both women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water and salt are minor ingredients that should be בטל in the flour. If so, the dough should follow only the flour's owner.
